$schema: Enjin Engine trust/security zone map for AI-assisted development
$purpose: Machine-readable boundary annotations so AI models can gauge risk, enforce validation, and avoid accidental security regressions when navigating the codebase.

security-critical.description: Handles untrusted input, network data, user-supplied file paths, script execution, or DLL loading. Every parameter must be validated. Changes here require security review.

trust-boundary.description: Transition points where untrusted data crosses into trusted engine state. Input validation, bounds checking, and sanitization MUST happen here. If adding a new boundary, follow the validation patterns in existing ones.
rules: Validate all integer ranges before casting enums
Bounds-check array indices and allocation sizes from deserialized data
Sanitize file paths — reject or neutralize '..' traversal
Cap recursion/iteration depth to prevent stack overflow or DoS
Check stream/file I/O return values (tellg, tellp, read, write)

user-api.description: Public API surface exposed to game developers via AngelScript bindings and Visual Script nodes. Changes here affect the scripting contract — additions are safe, removals/renames break user scripts.
rules: New bindings: add freely; removals/renames break existing game scripts
All parameters from scripts are untrusted — validate at the binding layer

editor-internal.description: Editor UI code (ImGui panels, tools, dialogs). Only the engine developer interacts with this — not exposed to game scripts or end-user players. Lower risk than security-critical, but still processes file paths and JSON configs.

renderer-internals.description: Low-level Vulkan/GPU code. No direct user input reaches here — data arrives pre-validated from ECS components. Risk is GPU resource leaks, driver crashes from malformed Vulkan calls, or memory corruption from bad buffer math.
rules: Cast to VkDeviceSize before multiplying dimensions for buffer sizes
Verify memory type index compatibility for each image/buffer format
Reset descriptor cache state at render pass boundaries

gameplay-runtime.description: Runtime gameplay systems (physics, audio, AI, save/load, dialogue, quests). Data comes from ECS components set up by the editor or scripts. Moderate trust — values should be in reasonable ranges but aren't adversarial.
rules: Cap iteration counts and allocation sizes (e.g., max debris, max particles)
Guard against divide-by-zero in resolution/grid calculations
Limit recursion depth for chain reactions and graph execution

foundation.description: Core math, memory, logging, platform abstraction. Shared by everything. Changes here have the widest blast radius. No untrusted input arrives directly.

deserialization: Validate enum integer values against valid ranges before casting
Clamp numeric values to reasonable min/max
Cap array/vector sizes from untrusted sources
Return safe defaults for malformed data
file-paths: Use std::filesystem::weakly_canonical() to resolve path before comparison
Verify resolved path starts with expected base directory
vulkan-resources: Check VkResult after every vkCreate*/vkAllocate*/vkBind* call
Re-query memory type index per format (don't reuse across different formats)
Use VkDeviceSize for all size arithmetic to prevent u32 overflow
Clean up partially-created resources on failure (don't leak VkImage/VkDeviceMemory)
recursion-and-loops: Add depth counter to all recursive graph/tree traversals
Cap maximum iteration count for unbounded loops over untrusted data
Use thread_local depth guards for re-entrant execution paths
